basic.title: Introduction to Law
basic.overview: Learn how rules are applied to real situations.

lesson.title: Rules meet facts
paragraphs: Law is not only a list of rules. The main skill is applying a rule to a set of facts and explaining why it fits.

Take a sign in a park that says “No vehicles.” Does a bicycle count? What about a toy car, or an ambulance in an emergency? Reasonable people can disagree, so lawyers look at the purpose of the rule and its exact words.
Law students practise this by reading short cases and explaining their reasoning step by step.

basic.realWorld: Lawyers spend much of their time deciding how a rule applies to a client’s particular facts.

task.prompt: A sign says “No vehicles in the park.” Is a bicycle allowed? Give your reasoning in two or three sentences.
task.note: There is no single correct answer. Showing your reasoning is what legal training practises.

medium.title: Contracts
medium.overview: Learn how agreements become legally binding promises.

lesson.title: When is a promise binding?
paragraphs: A contract is an agreement the law will enforce. In many legal systems, lawyers look at whether there was a clear offer, whether it was accepted, and whether both sides meant to be bound.
Rules differ from country to country, so lawyers always check the law that applies to their case.
You will practise reading an agreement closely, spotting unclear wording, and asking what each side actually promised.

medium.realWorld: Companies, landlords, and employers all use contracts, and many lawyers draft or review them every day.

task.prompt: Maya texts Dani: “I will sell you my bike for 500,000.” Dani replies: “Deal.” What would a lawyer ask first?
options: Was there a clear offer and a clear acceptance?
How old are Maya and Dani?
Which of them owns a nicer bike?
task.note: Lawyers usually start by asking what was agreed and whether it was clear. Careful questions come before conclusions.

deep.title: Legal Clinic
deep.overview: See how lawyers help real people with real problems.

lesson.title: Listening before advising
paragraphs: In a legal clinic, students meet people who need help. The first job is listening, then separating facts from feelings and finding what is still unknown.
Only after that do you look for the rules that apply and explain the options in plain language.
Students often work under a supervising lawyer, who reviews every document before it is sent.

deep.realWorld: Interns at law firms and legal aid centres often prepare case files and draft letters for a lawyer to review.

task.prompt: A tenant says the landlord keeps entering the flat without warning. Write two questions you would ask before giving any advice.
task.note: There is no right answer. Good questions about the facts come before any advice.
